subfield: Plasma physics / laser-plasma interaction and accelerator physics
motivation: Tajima's theoretical proposal (with the late John Dawson, 1979) that an intense laser pulse can drive a plasma wake with accelerating fields a thousand times stronger than conventional radio-frequency cavities opened an entirely new field of plasma physics. Malka and Leemans turned this idea into reality: Malka's group demonstrated quasi-monoenergetic electron beams (2004) and controlled optical injection, and Leemans' team at Berkeley produced GeV-class beams in centimetre-scale plasma channels, later reaching nearly 8 GeV in 20 cm. This is rigorous nonlinear kinetic plasma theory made quantitative and predictive, tamed despite the messy physics of real plasmas, and now driving compact X-ray sources, free-electron lasers and applications in medicine and materials science. Laser wakefield acceleration is a genuine paradigm shift in how we accelerate particles, rooted in fundamental plasma physics.
